title: Bài sưu tầm 133 - Passage 1: Mary Anning: The Fossil Hunter of Lyme Regis
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 1 — TEST 133

Mary Anning: The Fossil Hunter of Lyme Regis

Paragraph 1. Born in 1799 in the coastal town of Lyme Regis in southern England, Mary Anning grew up in difficult circumstances. Her father, Richard, was a struggling cabinetmaker who supplemented his modest earnings by gathering strangely shaped stones along unstable sea cliffs and selling them from a street table to wealthy summer visitors.

Paragraph 2. When Richard died in 1810, leaving behind unpaid debts and no savings, his children kept searching the rocky beach for income. In 1811, Mary's older brother Joseph spotted a four-foot skull protruding from the shale, and Mary then spent months carefully chiselling out the rest of the skeleton—later named Ichthyosaurus, or 'fish-lizard', by scholars in London.

Paragraph 3. Searching the crumbling cliffs after winter storms was hazardous work. In 1833, Anning narrowly escaped death when a sudden rockfall killed her loyal terrier dog, Tray, just metres from where she stood. Yet despite working in freezing rain without formal schooling, she became an extraordinary observer. To understand extinct creatures, she dissected modern ocean animals such as squid and fish, and prepared remarkably precise anatomical diagrams of her discoveries.

Paragraph 4. In 1823, Anning uncovered Britain's first complete Plesiosaurus, a marine reptile with an astonishingly long neck. Its proportions seemed so improbable that the renowned French anatomist Georges Cuvier initially declared the specimen a clever forgery assembled from separate animals. After inspecting Anning’s detailed notes and sketches, however, Cuvier publicly withdrew his accusation and acknowledged the fossil as genuine.

Paragraph 5. Five years later, she found Britain's first winged reptile, a pterosaur, and realised that stony lumps known as 'bezoar stones' were actually fossilised faeces that revealed ancient diets. Nevertheless, recognition rarely followed. As a working-class woman, Anning was barred from joining the all-male Geological Society of London. Wealthy scholars bought her specimens and published descriptions in prestigious journals while seldom mentioning the woman who had excavated and prepared them.

Paragraph 6. By the final decade of her life, leading scientists from across Europe travelled to consult Anning at her tiny Lyme Regis fossil shop. In 1838, the British Association arranged a modest annual pension to ease her financial strain. Today, historians regard this self-taught collector as one of the true pioneers of modern paleontology.

groups.title: Questions 8–13
groups.instructions:
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 8–13 on your answer sheet, write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.

steps: Đoạn 1: "selling them... to wealthy summer visitors" (affluent seasonal = wealthy summer).
Đoạn 2: "leaving behind unpaid debts and no savings".
Đoạn 3: "a sudden rockfall killed her loyal terrier dog".
Đoạn 4: "initially declared the specimen a clever forgery".

q8.text: Collecting fossils was not Richard Anning's primary occupation.

steps: Đoạn 1: Nghề chính của ông là thợ đóng tủ (cabinetmaker); việc nhặt hóa thạch chỉ để kiếm thêm thu nhập (supplemented his modest earnings).

q9.text: Mary Anning discovered the entire first Ichthyosaurus skeleton entirely on her own.

steps: Đoạn 2: Anh trai Joseph là người đầu tiên phát hiện phần hộp sọ dài 4 foot, sau đó Mary mới đục tách phần thân còn lại.

q10.text: Anning learned how to dissect sea creatures from medical books lent by London scholars.

steps: Đoạn 2 & 3: Bài nhắc học giả London và việc Mary tự giải phẫu sinh vật biển hiện đại, nhưng không hề nói cô học kỹ thuật này từ sách y học mượn của họ hay tự mày mò.

q11.text: Georges Cuvier refused to alter his view of the Plesiosaurus even after inspecting Anning's drawings.

steps: Đoạn 4: Sau khi xem bản vẽ và ghi chú của Mary, Cuvier đã công khai rút lại cáo buộc giả mạo và công nhận hóa thạch là thật.

q12.text: The Geological Society of London excluded female members throughout Anning's lifetime.

steps: Đoạn 5: "barred from joining the all-male Geological Society of London".

q13.text: Anning's Lyme Regis shop attracts more modern visitors than the museum displays of her fossils.

steps: Đoạn 6: Bài nhắc cửa hàng nhỏ ở Lyme Regis khi xưa các học giả đến thăm, không hề so sánh lượng khách tham quan ngày nay.
